gate1_third_model_family_INTACT.summary: 0/3 INTACT non-OLMo families show letter-interface failure. Llama-2-7B letter 0.4100 (+14.11pp vs always-D 0.2689), Llama-3-8B 0.6220 (+35.31pp), Qwen3-8B-Base 0.7464 (+47.75pp). All n=14042, 0 nan. On Llama-3 and Qwen3 letter is 16-23pp BETTER than content.
gate1_third_model_family_INTACT.why_superseded: A01's kill claim is about DAMAGED models. Intact bases were never expected to show the pathology; measuring them cannot trigger or clear the kill clause. GATE1_VERDICT.md's 'kill clause 2 triggered / narrow to OLMo-only' conclusion was WRONG and is retracted -- see gate1_third_model_family_DAMAGED.
gate1_third_model_family_INTACT.still_useful_for: the second-order observation that on three of four HEALTHY strong models the letter interface is substantially BETTER than the label-free content interface (+13 to +23pp), so 'content is the fair interface' is not a general statement about MC interfaces
gate1_third_model_family_INTACT.evidence: GATE1_VERDICT.md (keep for the intact numbers; its verdict section is retracted), evidence/a01_gate1_third_family.json

gate1_third_model_family_DAMAGED.summary: 6/6 DAMAGED non-OLMo arms land at/below their own best-constant floor 0.2689. Llama-2 k8 0.2415 (-2.74pp), Llama-3 k8 0.2329 (-3.60), Qwen3 k8 0.2286 (-4.03), Llama-2 k12 0.2295 (-3.94), Llama-3 k12 0.2527 (-1.62), Qwen3 k12 0.2300 (-3.89). Damage = front-N truncation, NO fresh block, NO heal (deliberately worst-case).
gate1_third_model_family_DAMAGED.mechanism_finding: The collapse ROUTE differs by family but the OUTCOME does not. Non-OLMo damaged arms become constant-letter emitters with NEAR-ZERO exact ties (Llama-2 k12 is 100.0% modal with 0.00% ties; Qwen3 k12 is 99.1% modal with 0.03% ties). OLMo damaged arms reach the same place via 30.64% exact ties + argmax index tie-breaking. So ties are ONE road, not THE mechanism -- this over-determines the gate-3 refutation.
gate1_third_model_family_DAMAGED.content_also_fails: every damaged arm has content_norm within +/-3pp of its letter accuracy and both hover at their floors -- switching interface does NOT rescue a damaged arm

gate1_depth_curve.verdict: THE TWO INTERFACES HAVE DIFFERENT FUNCTIONAL FORMS -- letter is a STEP function of depth, content_norm is SMOOTH and MONOTONE
gate1_depth_curve.ran: 2026-08-08/09, four families across .21/.73/.82; 58 arms x 14042 items, thresholds pinned to a single layer
gate1_depth_curve.headline: Letter accuracy sits pinned at its 0.2689 floor over a wide depth range, then jumps 27-48pp at ONE layer, then plateaus. Content_norm over the SAME forward passes rises smoothly and monotonically with no jump anywhere. At the layer where Qwen3 letter moves +48.0pp (k24 0.2297 -> k25 0.7099), Qwen3 content moves +1.4pp (0.3045 -> 0.3180).

thresholds_pinned.qwen3_8b_36L: k24->k25, +48.0pp. Pinned at 0.2295-0.2301 for k=4..24 -- twenty depths agreeing within 0.06pp
thresholds_pinned.relative_depth: thresholds at k/L = 0.69 / 0.56 / 0.59 -- past the midpoint in all three, but n=3, NOT a law

gate1_depth_curve.llama2_anomaly: letter NON-MONOTONE (k16 0.3289 +6.0pp -> k20 0.3054 -> k24 0.2723 +0.3pp back at floor -> k28 0.4315) while content over the same range is STRICTLY monotone (0.2650->0.2877->0.3139->0.3548). The non-monotonicity is in the readout, not the model. Gap-fill k=8,12,18,22,26 in flight on .21. Also: Llama-2's k28 letter 0.4315 already exceeds its INTACT 0.4100, so its plateau is at intact level -- it is a weak-model case, not a damage case.
gate1_depth_curve.why_it_matters: Supplies a mechanism-free version of A01's protocol argument. Below threshold the letter interface IS a constant predictor; above it, a competent one. Averaging arms that straddle the threshold mixes two regimes. Any damage-scaling regression on letter accuracy that includes sub-threshold rungs is fitting a step, and its slope is an artifact of how many rungs land on each side. This also EXPLAINS the 6/6 damaged result: those arms were keep8/keep12, deep inside every family's sub-threshold range.
gate1_depth_curve.does_not_show: no mechanism (tie explanation stays triple-falsified, this does not resurrect it); nothing about HEALED arms (all arms here are truncation-only); no per-subject breakdown
gate1_depth_curve.ops_note: .21's .venv/bin/python is a broken symlink to a torch-less py3.11; use /opt/conda/envs/torch-base/bin/python on .21 too

gate2_second_mc_benchmark.summary: On non-MMLU MC the interface/floor failure DOES reproduce. BoolQ's construct-appropriate null is 0.6217 (always-B), not 0.5: keep12/keep10/keep8 all sit BELOW it on the raw-LL interface and keep14 is n.s. (p=0.20) -> 4/6 arms indistinguishable from a constant predictor while their nominal 0.59-0.64 look 'passing' against a 0.50 chance line. OpenBookQA: longest-option null 0.3635 vs chance 0.2500; keep10 acc_norm 0.3560 is below that floor, and 3/15 arm-pair sign flips between acc and acc_norm. Residual fraction for base OBQA drops 45.9% -> 21.3% under the correct null (2.15x inflation from using chance).
gate2_second_mc_benchmark.caveat: The two interfaces used here are raw sum-LL vs length-normalised acc_norm, NOT MMLU's letter-vs-content. Report that difference explicitly; it is an analogous but not identical interface contrast.
gate2_second_mc_benchmark.negative_control: winogrande is structurally degenerate (both options share the continuation -> identical norm_lens, acc == acc_norm exactly, 100% tie rate). Cannot serve as an interface case; report as a control, not evidence.
gate2_second_mc_benchmark.clean_cases: CommonsenseQA (5-way) and SocialIQA (3-way): all 6 arms significantly ABOVE their constant-letter nulls on both interfaces -- the 'not everything collapses' side of the protocol.

gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.verdict: ALL SIX ARMS DONE. Ties are NOT the mechanism: fp32 eliminates every exact tie and changes no arm's floor verdict except one marginal case.
gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.stale_verdict_corrected_20260809: this field read 'base arm DONE; keep8 arm running on .73'. Both halves were stale -- keep8 finished AND four further arms were run. All six dtype_summary.json exist under results/a01_gate3/dtype_runs/ on zwfy6, and `ps` on .73 shows no A01 process. Four arms of completed evidence were sitting unreported.

7B_keep12_step124000.fp32_verdict: above the floor -- THE ONE FLIP, see below

gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.headline_1_fp32_kills_all_ties: fp32 drives the exact-tie rate to 0.00% on five of six arms (shortgpt16 0.01%), from a bf16 rate that rises monotonically with damage to 30.64% on keep8. The ties are unambiguously a bf16 artifact.
gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.headline_2_verdicts_do_not_move: removing every tie leaves the floor verdict unchanged on 5/6 arms. keep8 stays BELOW and gets MORE significant (bf16 -1.389pp p=0.0192 -> fp32 -1.538pp p=0.0062). This is the triple-falsification of 'ties are the mechanism', now at n=6 arms instead of 2.

the_one_flip_keep12_MARGINAL.do_not_overclaim: ONE arm of six; the fp32 CI clears zero by 0.078pp; p=0.0272 is UNCORRECTED and would not survive BH across the six arms. Report as 'one arm's verdict is dtype-fragile at the margin', NOT as 'fp32 rescues keep12'. It argues for reporting dtype alongside every verdict -- which is A01's own thesis -- not for a mechanism claim.
the_one_flip_keep12_MARGINAL.modal_shift_cuts_the_other_way: keep12's modal-letter concentration RISES under fp32: D@49.3% -> D@61.3%. So fp32 nudges accuracy up while making the arm a MORE degenerate constant predictor. The two move in opposite directions.

gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.headline_3_fp32_makes_damaged_arms_more_: modal concentration rises under fp32 on every damaged arm: keep10 D 60.1->65.1%, keep12 D 49.3->61.3%, keep8 C 48.8->55.9%. Removing index tie-breaking does not make a damaged arm less degenerate -- it makes it more visibly constant. Worth a sentence in the paper.
gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.base_arm_result: fp32 removes ALL exact ties (18 -> 0) but letter acc is UNCHANGED: 0.6054 both dtypes, delta +0.0000 CI95 [-0.0011,+0.0011], McNemar p=1.000. 96 letter argmax flips (0.68%), of which only 12 were the bf16-tied items. So on the intact model, ties are a bf16 artifact AND removing them changes nothing measurable.
gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.note: gate-1's Llama-2 result (15.79% ties, fully healthy) now serves as an external positive control for 'ties without failure', which reframes what the keep8 arm can show.
gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.evidence: results/a01_gate3/dtype_runs/{7B_base,7B_shortgpt16_step200000,7B_keep14_step200000,7B_keep12_step124000,7B_keep10_step83500,7B_keep8_step121000}_dtype/dtype_summary.json -- all on zwfy6 ONLY, wzc1 does not have them

claim_scope_after_gates.RETRACTED_must_narrow: An earlier version of this file said 'drop any claim that the letter MC interface is GENERALLY an unreliable instrument'. RETRACTED: that was based on INTACT bases only. The damaged-arm gate (6/6 non-OLMo below floor) confirms the general claim.
claim_scope_after_gates.must_drop: 'Exact ties are the mechanism of interface failure' as a family-general CAUSAL claim. Triple-falsified: (a) gate-3 base, ties 18->0 in fp32, acc unchanged p=1.000; (b) gate-3 keep8, ties 4303->0, 18% argmax flips, acc unchanged p=0.570, still below floor; (c) damaged non-OLMo collapse to the same place with 0.00-1.35% ties.
confirmed_general: Under structural damage the letter MC interface degenerates to at/below its own best-constant floor. Demonstrated on FOUR families: OLMo-2-7B (healed keep8, 0.2550), Llama-2-7B (trunc, 0.2295-0.2415), Llama-3-8B (trunc, 0.2329-0.2527), Qwen3-8B-Base (trunc, 0.2286-0.2301).
The collapse is a SHARP phase transition in depth, not a gradual decay -- Qwen3 is pinned at 0.2297 for keep 4..24 then jumps +45.74pp at keep30.
Interface swap does NOT rescue a damaged arm: content_norm sits within +/-3pp of letter on every damaged arm.

Report every construct against a construct-appropriate null (best-constant, not chance) before comparing arms. Demonstrations: keep8 0.2550 reads 'above chance' at .25 but is BELOW the 0.2689 floor; BoolQ 0.59-0.64 reads 'passing' at .50 but is below the 0.6217 always-B floor; OBQA residual fraction inflates 2.15x under the chance line.
gate-2's non-MMLU replication: the wrong-null problem is not an MMLU artifact.
The self-falsification narrative (using the protocol to retract one's own headline) -- now including this file's own retraction of the intact-only verdict.
family_specific_not_general: The collapse MECHANISM. OLMo-2 gets there via exact bf16 ties (30.64% on keep8) resolved by argmax index bias; Llama/Qwen get there via direct modal collapse with near-zero ties. Same destination, different road.

On HEALTHY strong models the letter interface is substantially BETTER than the label-free content interface (+13 to +23pp on OLMo-2 base, Llama-3, Qwen3). So 'content is the fair interface' is not a general statement about MC interfaces -- it is a statement about damaged models.
